clue.text: One seen in rank Scorsese movie?

definitions.meaning: someone found waiting at a cab rank for fares
the 1976 Martin Scorsese film starring Robert De Niro

explanation.surface: A film buff spots someone in the ranks and wonders whether it is a Scorsese picture.
explanation.walkthrough: A taxi rank is the British name for a cab stand, where cabs queue for passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a cabbie waits at a rank, and Scorsese directed the famous film of that title.

clue.text: With which to spray a flipping sore boil regularly?

indicators.note: the word sore is flipped to read the other way
every other letter of boil is taken

explanation.surface: What do you spray on a painful boil?
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns SORE into EROS; 'regularly' takes O and L from boil. 'flipping' poses as a mild British curse.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressurised can that releases a fine mist is the device used for spraying.

clue.text: Castro had ideas about seizing a state

indicators.note: about indicates the held letters turn round
the words Castro had ideas seize, or hold, the letters wanted

explanation.surface: Fidel Castro had plans to take over a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizing' finds OHADI in castrO HAD Ideas; 'about' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the fifty United States, in the northwest and known for potatoes.

clue.text: Stir treacle, taking time — it should be runny

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in, or contain, the letter for time
stirring treacle mixes it, so its letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Instructions to stir treacle slowly until it flows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' rearranges TREACLE and 'taking' adds T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: This Swiss dish of cheese is melted and scraped off in a molten, flowing state, so it should be runny.

clue.text: Fresh Venice calamari, line caught, served very cold

indicators.note: the letter for line is caught inside the rearranged letters
a fresh arrangement of the letters of Venice calamari

explanation.surface: A seafood menu: fresh calamari from Venice, line-caught, served chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' anagrams VENICE CALAMARI; 'caught' puts L inside. 'line caught' looks like a fishing method.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen dessert must be served chilled; this flavour is the plainest and most popular of them.

clue.text: Nice street almost packed — sorry!

parts.note: rue is French for street, as in the city of Nice

indicators.note: the word for packed is not quite complete, its final letter missing

parts.note: packed means full

explanation.surface: An apology that a street in Nice is nearly packed with people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, so the street is French: RUE. 'almost' drops the last L of FULL.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling or expressing regret, a sorry look is regretful.

clue.text: Solid snooker player uses it potting black

indicators.note: potting a ball sinks it into a pocket, so here the letter is sunk inside the other piece

parts.note: a snooker player strikes the balls with a cue
B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A snooker player pots the black ball with a solid shot of the cue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potting' puts B inside CUE.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a solid figure with six square faces is one example of a three-dimensional solid.

clue.text: Fashionable at last, it gave Sarkozy a lift

definitions.text: Fashionable at last, it gave Sarkozy a lift

parts.words: Fashionable at last, it gave Sarkozy a lift
parts.note: a raised boot heel came back into fashion, and the short French president was known to wear heightened shoes

explanation.walkthrough: Nicolas Sarkozy, a short French president, was mocked for wearing built-up shoes; a 'lift' is extra height.
explanation.definitionFit: This tall, tapered men's heel gives extra height, the sort of boost a short politician might want.

clue.text: For him, work is a constant grind

definitions.text: For him, work is a constant grind

parts.words: For him, work is a constant grind
parts.note: a coffee shop worker grinds beans all day, a literal grind

explanation.walkthrough: 'grind' reads as drudgery, but it is literal: grinding coffee beans.
explanation.definitionFit: A café employee who makes espresso drinks spends the shift grinding coffee.

clue.text: Song penned by Robin's girl

indicators.note: the wanted letters are enclosed, as if in a pen, by the name, so its outer letters are dropped

parts.note: Maid Marian is the sweetheart of Robin Hood

explanation.surface: A song written by the girlfriend of someone called Robin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' means the answer sits inside MARIAN, so its first and last letters, M and N, go.
explanation.definitionFit: An operatic solo piece for a single voice is a kind of song.

clue.text: Run to purchase last bit of beer bottled in holy city

parts.note: a canter is an easy run for a horse

indicators.note: beer bottled in another word means its letter is held inside it

parts.note: to purchase is to buy

indicators.note: the final letter of the word beer is taken

explanation.surface: Someone dashes out to buy the last of the beer bottled in a sacred city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottled' puts R, the last letter of beer, inside BUY.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral city is the seat of the Archbishop and the mother church of Anglicanism, a holy place of pilgrimage.

clue.text: Landed aristocracy's first to provide support

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word aristocracy is used

parts.note: to shore up is to prop or support

explanation.surface: The landed gentry's leading member props everything up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landed' looks like the gentry adjective, but here it means come to land.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors who have landed are on dry land, out of the ship and on the beach.

clue.text: Backing Essen duo loath to restrict sound level

indicators.note: Backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
the words Essen duo loath restrict, or hold within them, the letters wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A reluctant pair from the German city of Essen are unwilling to keep the volume down.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'to restrict' into the definition, but those words are the hidden-word signal; the definition is just 'sound level'.
explanation.definitionFit: Volume, the strength of a noise as heard, is its sound level.

clue.text: Ordering BLT, a cake, Darjeeling for one

indicators.note: putting the letters in a fresh order rearranges them

parts.note: taken as written: a bacon, lettuce and tomato sandwich plus a cake

explanation.surface: At a café someone orders a bacon sandwich, a cake and a Darjeeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordering' looks like placing a café order; it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Darjeeling is an example of a fermented, dark leaf brew drunk without milk or with it.

clue.text: Gregarious Vince suppressing unhappy blub

indicators.note: the surname holds down, or contains, the rearranged letters

parts.note: Vince Cable is a former leader of the Liberal Democrats

indicators.note: the letters of blub are unhappy, so put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A politician called Vince holds back a sad sob.
explanation.walkthrough: Vince Cable is a British Liberal Democrat politician, a former Business Secretary; 'unhappy' signals the anagram and 'suppressing' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Sociable enough to be a welcome member of a club, so gregarious and companionable.

clue.text: Hairy fellow's son seated in Emirates on the way back

indicators.note: the whole is read in the reverse direction
the letter for son sits inside the abbreviation for the Emirates

parts.note: UAE is the United Arab Emirates
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A hairy man's son has a seat on a flight back from the Emirates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seated in' puts S into UAE to give UASE; 'on the way back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Jacob's twin brother was a hirsute man, the Bible's best-known hairy fellow.

clue.text: Italian speciality suit tailored to go over — essentially — big butt

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go over, or around, the other pieces
a suit is tailored, reshaped, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to butt with the head is to ram

indicators.note: the essence of big is its central letter

explanation.surface: A tailored suit has to be let out to fit over a large backside after eating dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailored' makes TISU; 'butt' is the verb, as a goat butts, not a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffee-soaked layered dessert with mascarpone is a famous speciality of Italy.

clue.text: Soviet spies arresting university teacher

indicators.note: the spies arrest, or hold, the letter for university

parts.note: the GRU is the Soviet (now Russian) military intelligence service

explanation.surface: Soviet agents detain a university lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arresting' puts U inside GRU.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiritual guide or mentor in Hindu tradition is a teacher of disciples.

clue.text: Arthur, drunk, catching Edgware's last Tube

indicators.note: the jumbled name catches the final letter of Edgware inside it
Arthur is drunk, so his letters stagger out of order
the final letter of Edgware is taken

explanation.surface: Drunken Arthur makes the last Underground train from Edgware.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgware is a London suburb at the end of a Tube (London Underground) line. 'drunk' rearranges ARTHUR; 'catching' puts E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The duct carrying urine out of the bladder is an anatomical tube.

clue.text: Relax belt while undressed inside

indicators.note: the stripped letters go inside the word for belt

parts.note: to belt someone is to clout them

indicators.note: the word while has its outer letters stripped off

explanation.surface: Someone loosens their belt and relaxes after getting undressed indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belt' is the blow, not the strap; 'undressed' strips the outer letters off 'while'.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwind is the informal phrasal verb meaning take it easy and stop worrying.

clue.text: Parcel firm profit good in period of economic growth

parts.note: UPS, United Parcel Service, is a delivery company
to win is to gain or profit

explanation.surface: A parcel company's good profits during a boom.
explanation.definitionFit: An upward turn in business activity or the economy is an improvement or recovery.

clue.text: Leader of Taunton beer enthusiasts serving up the black stuff!

indicators.note: the first letter of Taunton leads the word
in a down clue, up means the letters are read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: CAMRA, the Campaign for Real Ale, is a British group of beer lovers

explanation.surface: A Taunton real-ale club chief pours a pint of Guinness, the black stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the black stuff' is a nickname for Guinness, but here it is road surfacing. Taunton is a town in Somerset. 'serving up' reverses CAMRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt road surfacing is black, so 'the black stuff' fits it as a playful description.

clue.text: Bugs infesting caramel blancmange?

indicators.note: insects infesting a pudding live inside it, so the answer lies within these words

explanation.surface: Is a caramel blancmange crawling with insects?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugs' is not insects but Bugs Bunny, whose voice actor's name is hidden here.
explanation.definitionFit: The American voice artist who gave Bugs Bunny his voice can be named by his famous character.

clue.text: Majestic gold sports car American imported

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: the American letters are brought into the car's letters

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, labels a sports car

explanation.surface: A majestic gold sports car is imported from America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imported' signals the container: the American letters go inside the car's.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means stately, grand and inspiring awe, a synonym of majestic.

clue.text: Donated large hammer

parts.note: to donate is to give, past tense gave
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.definitionFit: An auctioneer or judge bangs a small wooden mallet, a ceremonial hammer.

clue.text: ANC politician forcing Keith to transport nuclear device

indicators.note: to transport something is to carry it, so the rearranged name carries the bomb within
Keith is forced out of shape, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: an A-bomb is an atomic bomb

explanation.surface: An ANC politician is coercing someone called Keith into smuggling an atomic weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forcing' rearranges the name to THEKI, and 'to transport' carries the bomb inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: He succeeded Nelson Mandela as South Africa's president, a leading figure of the African National Congress.

clue.text: Arrogant article plugging wine from Bordeaux

indicators.note: the article plugs a gap in the middle of the French wine word

parts.note: vin is French for wine
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A haughty piece of writing promotes a Bordeaux wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugging' puts A inside VIN. 'plugging' looks like advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone conceited, with too high an opinion of themselves, is arrogant.

clue.text: At work, discontented, engaged by iron forge

indicators.note: the outer letters are held, as in a gear engaged, inside the symbol for iron

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: with its contents removed, only the outer letters of At work remain

explanation.surface: An unhappy worker is employed at an iron forge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forge' is to counterfeit, not a smithy; 'discontented' empties 'At work' and 'engaged by' sets what is left inside the iron symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To counterfeit a signature or banknote is to make a false copy, a synonym of forge.

clue.text: Cover Macau golf out east

indicators.note: letters that are out of place are jumbled

explanation.surface: Golf in Macau is cancelled, with play out in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles MACAU GOLF; E for east is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Disguise that hides something by blending it into its surroundings gives cover.
